result.document_summary: Los Angeles Housing Department bulletins (effective July 1, 2026) describing relocation assistance required for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO, and for demolition for new construction under the Resident Protections Ordinance.
result.notes: The bulletin is an agency summary of LAMC provisions. Only the no-fault eviction / relocation regime (one just_cause_eviction record for the RSO/JCO instrument, including Chart A amounts) and the separate RPO demolition-relocation regime are recorded. Admin fees, escrow mechanics and appeal fees are details and not separate records. The bulletin does not give the base RSO/JCO coverage tests (building age, unit counts), so coverage is left empty; coverage_text states it applies to units covered by the RSO or JCO. The RPO effective date of 2/11/2025 is the stated adoption date of the ordinance. The B bulletin fee chart is labeled 2025-26 while the A bulletin shows the same amounts for 2026-27; this does not affect the rules extracted.

rules.title: No-fault eviction relocation assistance under the RSO and JCO
rules.requirement: Before a no-fault eviction from a unit covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance or Just Cause Ordinance, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of serving the notice. Amounts depend on eligible/qualified status, length of tenancy and income, and are paid per unit.
rules.key_value: Eligible: $11,000 (<3 yrs) / $14,400 (3+ yrs or low income); Qualified: $23,150 / $27,400; single-family owned by natural person (JCO): one month's rent (effective July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027)
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD)
rules.coverage_text: Units covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) when the tenancy is ended for a no-fault reason.
rules.exemptions_text: No relocation assistance when evicting a resident manager to replace with another resident manager, or when required to evict due to natural-disaster hazardous conditions not caused by landlord negligence; landlord may offset accumulated rent (except for government orders to vacate); reduced amounts for qualifying Mom and Pop owner/family occupancy evictions.
rules.interaction: Demolition of a Protected Unit for new construction with a lower-income tenant is governed instead by the RPO and State Housing Crisis Act amounts; RSO/JCO amounts serve as the minimum.
yields_to: Housing Crisis Act (Cal. Gov. Code § 66300 et seq.)

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance: relocation and tenant protections for demolition for new construction
rules.requirement: When a Protected Unit is demolished for new construction, the owner must pay relocation under State Housing Crisis Act or City law, whichever is higher, with enhanced standardized payments for lower-income households, plus rights to remain up to 6 months, return, and first refusal.
rules.key_value: Standardized payment (Chart B): $115,480 extremely low / $96,750 very low / $87,450 low income
rules.citation: Los Angeles Ordinance Nos. 188481 and 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance); Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6
rules.quoted_span:
On February 11, 2025, the Los Angeles City Council adopted the RPO which codified and expanded upon 
replacement requirements and occupant protections of the HCA
rules.coverage_text: Protected Units (including all RSO units and units recently rent-restricted or occupied by lower-income households) that will be demolished for new construction; enhanced payments apply to lower-income households.

all_of.value: Protected Unit demolished for new construction
all_of.text: The RPO only applies to Protected Units that will be demolished for the purpose of new construction.

rules.interaction: Codifies and expands the State Housing Crisis Act protections; owner must pay the highest applicable amount under State and City law. Above-low-income households receive RSO/JCO Chart A amounts.
yields_to: Housing Crisis Act (Cal. Gov. Code § 66300 et seq.)
